task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-06-14, in the area of play-type labeling and data quality):
Any teammate DRIVE preceding a PNR raises PNR PPP.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

research_concepts: teammate DRIVE immediately preceding a PNR
play-type labeling from play-by-play action type and sub-type
derived possession records (initiator, play type, points)
sequential play-type effects on possession outcome
methodological_questions: Does the play-type label for a teammate DRIVE and for a PNR reflect the actual play, or is it an artifact of the initiation_type mapping and foul-ending possessions?
Does a teammate DRIVE preceding a PNR change the next possession's PPP after controlling for shooter quality, shot distance, lineup and possession context?
Is the sequential effect distinguishable from a placebo preceding play type (for example SPOT_UP or PUTBACK before PNR) and from regression to the mean?
Can labels derived from the possession outcome (points, fouls) be kept out of the PPP comparison to avoid leakage?

historical_evidence.finding: Play-type labeling audit of OTHER and DRIVE foul leakage. Recorded verdict: artifact_found. OTHER possessions show 36% foul endings with PPP inflated (FOUL_BUCKET). DRIVE sits 12pp below the foul benchmark (FOUL_LEAK). PNR shows a 22% foul rate. Only 335 of 50,668 possessions (0.7%) map to a real play type via initiation_type. Mechanism recorded as C_artifact. Validation recorded as NOT_RECORDED.

Sequential pair premium and defensive aftershock, 8/8 play types. After an opponent runs play type X, the next offensive play type Y scores above its unconditional H2 baseline, and each play type shows a defensive aftershock. Recorded all-games aftershock after success includes DRIVE +0.123 (n=57621) and PNR +0.127 (n=51194). The condition is opponent play type X, not a teammate DRIVE. [prior work] is limited by small sample ([prior work]).

Superstar sequential suppression: opponent play before the star. PUTBACK is the top suppressor for 6 or more stars (for example D. Mitchell d=-0.294, n_after=95). Recorded as having no multiplicity correction, with n_after of 32 to 95 in several PUTBACK cells. Mechanism recorded as E_unclear. Linked to a drift/nonstationarity risk.

Superstar suppression profiles, including Q5c sequential triggering. Verdict: rank-1 suppressor varies meaningfully across players. Rank-1 deltas are mostly within 1 to 2 SE with no multiple-comparison control. An OTHER artifact is flagged in [prior work].

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using the initiation_type field to assign play types to possessions, and reading PPP differences across play types as real efficiency.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as C_artifact: only 0.7% of 50,668 possessions map to a real play type. OTHER PPP is inflated by foul endings, and DRIVE and PNR foul rates distort their PPP. The apparent PPP differences are attributed to labeling and foul artifacts.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Per-star sequential suppression cells, read as evidence of specific preceding play types suppressing PPP.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as E_unclear with no multiplicity correction. Several PUTBACK cells rest on n_after of 32 to 95, and no validation was recorded.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Ranking rank-1 opponent-play suppressors per star.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as inconclusive (E_unclear). Rank-1 deltas are mostly within 1 to 2 SE and have no multiple-comparison control.

evidence_establishes: The play-type labels that a PNR or DRIVE depends on are not validated in this project's data. [prior work][prior work] records that initiation_type recovers a real play type for only 0.7% of possessions and that foul endings distort OTHER, DRIVE and PNR PPP.

Sequential play-type analyses in this project have been run, with per-cell sample sizes that can be small ([prior work][prior work], [prior work][prior work]), and none has been recorded as a validated teammate-DRIVE-to-PNR effect.
Sequential aftershock and pair-premium effects have been reported as supported across play types (FAM:[prior work]), but these conditions are opponent play types, not teammate DRIVE preceding PNR.
evidence_does_not_establish: No retrieved record tests a teammate DRIVE immediately preceding a PNR, so the direction and size of the question's effect are unknown from history.
No record shows the DRIVE and PNR labels are valid in the 2022-23 to 2025-26 data. The one label audit ([prior work][prior work]) found an artifact and recorded no validation.
Whether FAM:[prior work]'s pair premium holds for teammate-only sequences or for the question's specific pairing is not shown. The retrieved text is truncated, and I did not read the full record.
No record gives a power calculation for the teammate DRIVE to PNR contrast.
own_inferences: The question as posed needs a valid label for the immediately preceding teammate possession and for the PNR. The 0.7% initiation_type mapping in [prior work][prior work] means the current labels would select a very small and possibly non-random subset of possessions.
Foul-ending selection is likely correlated with DRIVE and PNR, so a naive PPP comparison will mix in free-throw and foul-ending possessions. This is a probable source of artifact.
Sequences in which a teammate DRIVE precedes a PNR may be selected by offensive context (fast breaks, lineups, shooter quality). Without controls, any PPP gap is confounded.

Per-cell sample sizes in the retrieved suppression analyses are of the order of dozens to hundreds, so a single-pairing teammate test could be underpowered unless it is pooled across the full league and seasons.
uncertainties: Full text of FAM:[prior work] and [prior work][prior work] was not read. Only truncated result text was returned, so pair-level results for DRIVE and PNR are not confirmed.
Whether the label problem in [prior work][prior work] has been fixed in the current data build is not recorded. [prior work]'s validation status is NOT_RECORDED.
The effect size of a teammate DRIVE on PNR PPP is unknown, so power cannot be computed from the retrieved evidence.
The 2025-26 playoffs are partial before 2026-06-21, so that segment cannot be used on the question date (2026-06-14).

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieved audit ([prior work][prior work], artifact) showed that the play-type labels underlying the question are not valid at the scale needed. That pushed the decision from a direct test to a stop-and-validate step. The sequential-effect records (FAM:[prior work], [prior work][prior work], [prior work][prior work]) added the multiplicity and small-cell warnings that shape the design below. They did not establish the teammate-DRIVE effect, so they did not justify proceeding as posed.

blocking_constraints.text: PNR and DRIVE labels are derived from the play-by-play, and the derivation is tied to outcome (points, fouls). The derived labels may encode the outcome being measured.
initiation_type maps only 0.7% of 50,668 possessions to a real play type ([prior work][prior work]). Labels for the teammate-DRIVE and PNR possessions are not validated.
Shooter quality, shot distance, lineup and possession context are likely to correlate with both the preceding DRIVE and the PNR PPP.
A teammate DRIVE immediately before a PNR may be a rare sequence. Cell sizes could be too small for useful power in a single player or team stratum.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved record tests a teammate DRIVE preceding a PNR. [prior work][prior work] is a labeling audit that found an artifact, so the play-type labels needed for the test are not established. FAM:[prior work] reports supported sequential aftershock and pair-premium effects, but for opponent play types and not teammate-only sequences. [prior work][prior work] and [prior work][prior work] are per-star suppression analyses that are not hypothesis tests or are inconclusive, and they lack multiplicity control.

risks.text: Only 0.7% of possessions map to a real play type via initiation_type ([prior work][prior work]). Labels for DRIVE and PNR are not validated.
Foul endings and points are used in the derivation of the play-type labels, which is a leakage path into the PPP outcome.

Foul-ending possessions have mechanically inflated or deflated PPP (OTHER 36% foul endings; DRIVE 12pp below foul benchmark; PNR 22% foul rate), which can produce an apparent effect with no basketball meaning.
Shooter quality, shot distance, lineup and possession context are not controlled in the question as posed.
Per-cell sample sizes in the retrieved suppression analyses are 32 to 95 for several cells ([prior work][prior work]), and the effect size of the teammate DRIVE to PNR contrast is unknown.
Many play-type pairs and players were scanned without multiplicity control ([prior work][prior work], [prior work][prior work]).
The result depends on a placebo or baseline preceding play type that has not been specified.
Labels and play-type definitions may change across the 2022-23 to 2025-26 seasons and between regular season and playoffs, as flagged in [prior work][prior work].

design.estimand: Do not run the teammate DRIVE to PNR contrast as posed yet. The first estimand is label validity: the share of possessions correctly assigned to DRIVE and PNR by an audited labeling rule (against a hand-checked sample). The conditional estimand, once labels pass, is the difference in next-possession PNR PPP (teammate DRIVE immediately before vs. matched baseline preceding play type), with the foul-ending contribution reported separately.
design.unit: Offensive possession by team, with the immediately preceding offensive possession by the same team. Possessions with fouls as the ending event are analysed separately or excluded from the PPP primary estimand.
design.sample: Regular seasons 2022-23 to 2025-26 (2025-26 regular season is complete from 2026-04-13). Playoffs 2022-23 to 2024-25. Exclude 2025-26 playoffs, which are partial on the question date of 2026-06-14 and complete only from 2026-06-21.
design.power: Not computable from the retrieved evidence. Run a simulation before analysis, using the league-wide PNR PPP and the empirical foul-ending rate, to fix the minimum detectable difference. Restrict the primary test to pooled league-level contrasts, not per-player cells.
design.controls: Possession-level covariates: shooter identity or quality, shot distance and result (from the play-by-play), lineup, game score margin, period and clock, and fast-break context. Use a mixed-effects model with random effects for team, game and player. Exclude foul-ending possessions from the primary PPP estimand and report them separately, so the outcome is not derived from fouls.
design.falsification: (1) Placebo preceding play types (SPOT_UP, PUTBACK, PULL_UP) before PNR should show no effect of the same size. (2) Reverse-order check: PNR before DRIVE should not predict DRIVE PPP. (3) Opponent DRIVE before PNR should be compared with teammate DRIVE to test whether the effect is specific to the teammate sequence.
design.multiplicity: Pre-register one primary contrast (teammate DRIVE before PNR, league-level, foul endings excluded). Treat the placebo and reverse-order checks as secondary, with Holm correction across all play-type pairs scanned.
design.decision_rule: Proceed to the primary test only if the label audit passes a pre-set accuracy threshold on a hand-checked sample. Then support the question only if the primary contrast is positive with a 95% CI excluding zero, and both placebo and reverse-order checks show no comparable effect. Otherwise report as uncertain or artifact.
design.data_version: 2022-23 to 2025-26 regular seasons (2025-26 complete from 2026-04-13) and 2022-23 to 2024-25 playoffs, using the current per-game files and the derived possession graph. Record the label-rule version and the audit result with the data version.
